material_systems.name: High-Build Latex Undercoater
material_systems.description: High-build latex primer/undercoater for factory-primed trim when additional primer coat is elected. Builds film thickness, levels minor surface imperfections, provides uniform base for finish coats.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start 046 High-Hiding Primer
products.notes: Optional primer over factory-primed trim. Factory primer is transit protection and often thin. High-build undercoater adds film thickness and levels surface. Scuff sand factory primer before application.

material_systems.compatibility_notes: Compatible with all acrylic, waterborne alkyd, and urethane finish systems. Factory primer must be scuff sanded (150-180 grit) and cleaned with tack cloth before application.

material_systems.name: MDF Edge Sealer (Solvent-Based)
material_systems.description: Solvent-based sealer for MDF edges ONLY. MANDATORY before any latex products on MDF edges. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber raise on MDF edges.

products.notes: Apply to MDF edges ONLY. Quick dry (15-30 min). Excellent edge seal. Alcohol cleanup.
Alternative to shellac. Longer dry time than shellac. Mineral spirits cleanup.

material_systems.compatibility_notes: MANDATORY DOCTRINE: MDF edges MUST receive solvent-based sealer before ANY latex products. This is Step 1 of a two-step process for bare MDF. Faces receive latex primer (SYS_MDF_FACE_PRIME) after edge seal.

material_systems.name: MDF Face Primer (Latex)
material_systems.description: High-build latex primer for MDF faces. Applied AFTER edges are sealed with solvent-based sealer. Builds film thickness and levels surface.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start 046 High-Hiding Primer
products.notes: Apply to MDF faces AFTER edges are sealed. High-build formula levels MDF surface. Sand faces 220 grit before prime.

material_systems.compatibility_notes: Step 2 of two-step MDF prime process. Edges must be sealed with SYS_MDF_EDGE_SEAL first. Compatible with all fine finish topcoat systems.

material_systems.name: Stain-Blocking Primer (FJP)
material_systems.description: Stain-blocking primer for Finger-Joint Pine (FJP). MANDATORY to prevent resin bleed-through. Without stain-blocking, amber/yellow discoloration will appear within weeks/months.

products.notes: BEST stain blocking. Blocks resin bleed, tannin, knots. Fast dry (15-45 min recoat). Alcohol cleanup. Strong odor — ventilation required.
Water-based alternative with good stain blocking. Lower odor than shellac. May require 2 coats on severe resin bleed. Water cleanup.
Excellent stain blocking. Longer dry time than shellac. Mineral spirits cleanup.

material_systems.compatibility_notes: MANDATORY DOCTRINE: FJP REQUIRES stain-blocking primer. This is NOT optional. Standard latex primers will NOT block resin. Shellac-based (BIN) provides best blocking; acrylic stain blockers (KILZ 3) acceptable for lighter resin loads.

material_systems.name: Standard Primer-Sealer
material_systems.description: Standard acrylic latex primer-sealer for bare solid wood trim (pine, poplar, etc.). Seals substrate, provides tooth for topcoat, blocks light stains.

products.notes: General purpose primer-sealer for bare wood. Good adhesion, moderate stain blocking. Water cleanup. Knots may require shellac spot prime.

material_systems.compatibility_notes: Compatible with all fine finish topcoat systems. For wood with visible knots or tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood), spot-prime knots with shellac (Zinsser BIN) before full primer coat.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer
material_systems.description: Bonding primer for glossy existing finishes or oil-based/alkyd existing finishes. Provides adhesion to low-porosity and chemically incompatible substrates.

example_products: INSL-X Stix Acrylic Waterborne Bonding Primer
products.notes: Waterborne bonding primer. Adheres to glossy surfaces without heavy sanding. Zero VOC available. Water cleanup.
Universal adhesion. Bonds to any surface including glossy and oil-based. Also blocks stains. Alcohol cleanup.

material_systems.compatibility_notes: For oil_based_existing substrates, perform adhesion test before full application. Degloss/sand (120-150 grit) before bonding primer. Clean surface thoroughly with solvent to remove contaminants.

material_systems.name: Shellac Knot Spot Primer
material_systems.description: Shellac-based spot primer for knots, tannin bleed, and localized stain blocking. Applied to specific defect areas before full primer coat.

products.notes: Apply to knots, resin pockets, and tannin stains before full primer coat. Aerosol convenient for spot work. Fast dry (15 min).

material_systems.compatibility_notes: Apply spot prime, allow to dry, then proceed with full primer system (SYS_STANDARD_PRIME or SYS_STAIN_BLOCK). Shellac is compatible under all topcoat systems.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Per PDCA standard: 1 LF trim = 1 SF. Simple profile (flat/square edge) has minimal surface area variation. Factory-primed substrate, standard absorption.
Per PDCA standard: 1 LF trim = 1 SF. Standard profile (ogee, cove) has typical surface area. 10% reduction from simple profile.
Complex/ornate profiles have increased surface area. 25% reduction from simple profile.
Edge sealer applied only to cut edges of MDF trim. Edge width typically 1/2" to 3/4". High absorption on raw MDF edge. Quart is typical purchase size for edge sealing.
MDF faces after edge seal. Simple profile. MDF is uniform porosity — consistent coverage.
MDF faces, complex/ornate profiles. Increased surface area.
FJP trim, simple profile. Bare wood absorbs more than factory-primed. Shellac-based products have higher solids — good coverage.
FJP trim, complex/ornate profiles. High surface area, high absorption.
Bare solid wood, simple profile. Standard absorption.
Glossy/oil-based existing finish. Low porosity = higher coverage. Simple profile.

consumables.name: 2-inch angled sash brush
consumables.specification: 2-inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle (nylon/polyester blend)
consumables.notes: Primary brush for trim priming. Angled sash for cutting in at wall line. Synthetic bristle for latex primers. ~5000 LF with proper care. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 1 brush per material type.

consumables.name: 2.5-inch angled sash brush
consumables.specification: 2.5-inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle (nylon/polyester blend)
consumables.notes: Larger brush for standard/complex profiles. Better coverage on wider trim. Synthetic bristle for latex.

consumables.name: Brush for shellac (dedicated)
consumables.specification: 2-inch angled sash brush, dedicated for shellac use, natural or synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Dedicated brush for shellac products (BIN, edge sealer). Shellac requires alcohol cleanup — keep separate from latex brushes. Natural bristle acceptable for shellac.

consumables.name: Spray tip 311 (primer)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 311 (6-inch fan, 0.011 orifice)
consumables.notes: Standard tip for primer on trim. 6-inch fan pattern for trim width. 0.011 orifice for primer viscosity.

consumables.name: Spray tip 413 (primer, wider fan)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 413 (8-inch fan, 0.013 orifice)
consumables.notes: Wider fan for taller trim (5.5"+ baseboard, crown molding). Larger orifice handles high-build primers.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons.

consumables.name: Sanding block fine (150-220 grit)
consumables.specification: Sanding block with fine grit range (150-220), rigid block construction
consumables.notes: Fine block for scuff sanding factory-primed trim, bare wood prep, and deglossing existing finishes. Rigid block per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.4.

consumables.name: Sanding block medium (100-150 grit)
consumables.specification: Sanding block with medium grit range (100-150), rigid block construction
consumables.notes: Medium block for bare substrate prep. MDF edges require more aggressive sanding (120 grit) to open pores before sealer.

consumables.name: Sandpaper sheet 120 grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 120 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: For MDF edge sanding. 120 grit opens pores for sealer penetration.

consumables.name: Sandpaper sheet 220 grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 220 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: For MDF face sanding and factory-primed scuff sand.

consumables.name: Sanding sponge fine
consumables.specification: Flexible sanding sponge, fine grit (180-220), angled edges
consumables.notes: For complex profiles only — carved details, rounded edges where rigid block cannot reach. Per doctrine: flexible sponge only for profile following, NOT defect leveling.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.specification: Paintable acrylic latex caulk, white, 10.1 oz tube
consumables.notes: For trim-to-wall joints, trim-to-trim miters, and gap filling. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: ~72 LF per tube for NC (consistent gaps, higher volume).

consumables.name: Caulk gun
consumables.specification: Standard caulk gun, ratchet-type
consumables.notes: Reusable tool for caulk application.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackling compound
consumables.specification: Lightweight spackling compound, tub or squeeze tube
consumables.notes: For fastener hole filling on trim. NC trim has high fastener count. Per doctrine: calculate NC trim fastener fill as separate line item based on trim LF. Approximately 2 holes per 12-16 inches of trim.

consumables.name: Wood filler (grain fill)
consumables.specification: Solvent-based or water-based wood filler for end grain
consumables.notes: For casing end grain fill on bare wood. Typically 2 ends per door opening, 4 per window opening.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.specification: Resin-impregnated cheesecloth for dust removal
consumables.notes: Wipe trim immediately before priming to remove sanding dust. Essential for quality finish. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.12.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth runner
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloth, 4x12 ft or 4x15 ft runner
consumables.notes: Perimeter floor protection during brush application. Reusable. Position along trim work area to catch drips.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.specification: 4 mil plastic sheeting for floor/wall protection
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for spray application. Heavier weight (4 mil) prevents tear during work.

consumables.name: Masking paper 12-inch
consumables.specification: Masking paper, 12-inch width, 180 LF roll
consumables.notes: For wall masking at trim edge during spray application. 180 LF per roll (60 yards). Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 1.5-inch
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 1.5-inch width
consumables.notes: For attaching masking paper to wall at trim edge. Also for floor protection seams. 180 LF per roll (60 yards).

consumables.name: Delicate surface tape (yellow)
consumables.specification: Delicate surface tape, 1.5-inch width, low tack
consumables.notes: Use when walls are already finish painted. Low tack prevents paint pull on removal. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.

consumables.name: Outlet/switch cover
consumables.specification: Plastic fixture covers or masking film squares
consumables.notes: Covers for electrical outlets and switches near spray zone.

consumables.name: Flexible putty knife
consumables.specification: Flexible putty knife, 1.5-inch or 2-inch
consumables.notes: For applying lightweight spackle to fastener holes. Flexible blade for flush fill.

consumables.name: Denatured alcohol
consumables.specification: Denatured alcohol for shellac cleanup
consumables.notes: For cleaning shellac from brushes and equipment. Required when using BIN or shellac sealers.

consumables.name: Mineral spirits
consumables.specification: Mineral spirits for oil-based product cleanup
consumables.notes: For cleaning oil-based sealers (KILZ Original, Cover Stain) from brushes. Also for surface cleaning on oil-based existing finishes.

material_notes.selection_guidance: Primer selection is driven by substrate_condition dimension, NOT quality tier. This is MANDATORY DOCTRINE per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 2.1. Each substrate type requires a specific primer chemistry. MDF requires TWO-STEP priming (solvent edge seal + latex face prime). FJP REQUIRES stain-blocking primer — this is non-negotiable.
material_notes.coverage_variability: Coverage rates are expressed per LF per PDCA standard (1 LF = 1 SF). Profile complexity affects coverage: simple profiles get better coverage, complex/ornate profiles consume more material. Bare substrates absorb more than factory-primed or previously painted surfaces.
material_notes.environmental_requirements: Follow manufacturer PDS for temperature and humidity requirements. Shellac products have strong odor — ensure adequate ventilation. Oil-based products require proper disposal of cleanup materials (see risk_notes).
material_notes.mdf_edge_warning: CRITICAL: MDF edges MUST receive solvent-based sealer (shellac or oil-based) BEFORE any latex products. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber raise on MDF edges. This is a two-step process: (1) seal edges, (2) prime faces.
material_notes.fjp_stain_block_warning: CRITICAL: FJP (Finger-Joint Pine) REQUIRES stain-blocking primer. Without stain-blocking, resin bleed-through will appear as amber/yellow discoloration within weeks/months. Standard latex primers will NOT block resin. Shellac-based (BIN) provides best blocking.

compatibility_rules.description: Never apply latex primer directly to raw MDF edges
compatibility_rules.consequence: Irreversible fiber raise, rough texture that sands poorly
compatibility_rules.resolution: Apply solvent-based sealer (SYS_MDF_EDGE_SEAL) first, then latex primer on faces only

compatibility_rules.description: Never use standard latex primer on bare FJP
compatibility_rules.consequence: Resin bleed-through within weeks/months, amber/yellow discoloration
compatibility_rules.resolution: Use stain-blocking primer (SYS_STAIN_BLOCK) - shellac-based or high-quality acrylic stain blocker

compatibility_rules.description: Latex topcoats may fail over oil-based existing finishes without bonding primer
compatibility_rules.resolution: Use bonding primer (SYS_BONDING_PRIME) after deglossing and adhesion test

risk_notes.description: Applying water-based primer to raw MDF edges before solvent-based sealer
risk_notes.consequence: Irreversible fiber raise requiring extensive sanding or replacement
risk_notes.mitigation: ALWAYS seal MDF edges with shellac-based or oil-based sealer FIRST

risk_notes.consequence: Amber/yellow discoloration within weeks/months that bleeds through finish coats
risk_notes.mitigation: ALWAYS use stain-blocking primer on bare FJP (shellac-based BIN preferred)

risk_notes.description: Painting over glossy or oil-based existing finish without proper prep
risk_notes.consequence: Adhesion failure requiring stripping and restart
risk_notes.mitigation: Adhesion test, thorough degloss/sand (120-150 grit), and bonding primer

risk_notes.description: Shellac products (BIN) have strong alcohol odor
risk_notes.consequence: Worker discomfort, potential health impact in enclosed spaces
risk_notes.mitigation: Ensure adequate ventilation. Use PPE (respirator) in enclosed spaces.

risk_notes.description: Oil-soaked rags can spontaneously combust during oxidative curing
risk_notes.mitigation: Place oil-soaked rags in water-filled metal container with lid. Dispose properly per local regulations.

risk_notes.description: Factory primer may be contaminated with oils, wax, or silicone from handling/shipping
risk_notes.mitigation: Scuff sand factory-primed surfaces (150-180 grit) and clean with tack cloth before additional primer or finish

assumptions.value: LF-based per PDCA standard (1 LF = 1 SF)

assumptions.source: Field estimate based on edge width and absorption
assumptions.note: No doctrine coverage for edge sealer quantity - derived from research. Marked for field validation.

assumptions.source: Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2 complexity modifiers applied to coverage
assumptions.note: Complexity modifiers in doctrine are for production rates, applied analogously to coverage.
